simple.meaning: כָּתַר (kâthar) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to enclose ; hence (in a friendly sense) to crown , (in a hostile one) to besiege ; also to wait (as restraining oneself).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 6 times across Judges, Job, Psalms, Proverbs, Habakkuk, beginning at Judges 20:43. Its contexts include righteousness, Torah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּתַר (H3803).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: כָּתַר (kâthar) / H3803 is traced through Judges 20:43, Job 36:2, Psalms 22:13, Psalms 142:8 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: They surrounded the Benjamites, chased them, and trod them down at their resting place, as far as near Gibeah toward the sunrise.

timeline.evidenceText: They surrounded the Benjamites, chased them, and trod them down at their resting place, as far as near Gibeah toward the sunrise.
“Bear with me a little, and I will show you;
They open their mouths wide against me,
Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails; for the wicked surround the righteous; therefore justice comes out perverted.

definitions.full: H3803. kathar [ כָּתַר ] verb surround (in Pi`el ), (Aramaic כַּתַּר Pa`el, wait, hope for; Pa`el wait, await, remain: i.e. perhaps surrounded expectantly , see Job 36:2 below) — Pi`el Perfect 3plural כִּתְּרוּ Judg 20:43 of surrounding an enemy; suffix כִּתְּרוּנִי Psa 22:13 (in figurative; || סְבָבוּנִי ); Imperative כַּתַּרלִֿי Job 36:2 wait, I pray (as in Aramaic) Hiph`il Imperfect 3masculine plural צַדִּיקִים יַכְּתִּרוּ בִּי Psalm 142:8 dubious, throw out crowns (Ges § 53g ), i.e. appear with crowns (denominative from כֶּתֶר ; but this very late — only in Esther); figurative for triumph , because of me; but Gr Che יִתְמָּֽאֲרוּ (see I. פאר ); דָ֑עַת יַכְתִּרוּ Prov 14:18 dubious, Thes De and others throw out knowledge as a crown , make knowledge their crown (denominative from כֶּתֶר ; but see above), Now, encompass knowledge , i.e. possess it (|| נָָֽחֲלוּ ); sense good, but meaning of ׳כ without ||. Participle מַכְתִּיר surrounding (as Pi`el ) Hab 1:4 (with accusative of enemy).
